content: The dose of brivaracetam should be increased by 100% (i.e., doubled) in patients receiving concurrent treatment with rifampin. Close monitoring is required. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of budesonide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Alternative therapies should be considered. Additionally, rifampin affects budesonide metabolism through CYP3A4, necessitating avoidance or substitution of the drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of buprenorphine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. This applies to buprenorphine in buccal, subdermal implant, and transdermal forms. For subdermal implants, if CYP3A4 inducers cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should transition to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. If the CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued, monitor for signs of overmedication. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of bupropion by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of buspirone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels of butabarbital and butalbital by increasing their metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If coadministration is necessary, increase the cabazitaxel dose and resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the inducer. Rifampin increases the metabolism of cabotegravir, reducing its systemic exposure and potentially leading to virologic failure. Coadministration is contraindicated. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If necessary, increase the cabozantinib dose and adjust back after discontinuing the inducer. Rifampin reduces caffeine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of calcifediol and calcitriol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Drugs that stimulate microsomal hydroxylation reduce the half-life of calcifediol. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. Calcium carbonate reduces rifampin absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. Monitor closely. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of canagliflozin by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. For patients with eGFR <73 mL/min/1.73 m², consider alternative antihyperglycemic agents. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust the dosage of CYP2B6 substrates as clinically appropriate. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers reduce capivasertib exposure, potentially decreasing efficacy. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of capmatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cariprazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to unclear effects on cariprazine exposure. Rifampin decreases carvedilol levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin reduces caspofungin levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ceftobiprole increases rifampin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/1B3 transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases celecoxib levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces cenobamate levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Adjust the dose of CYP2B6 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. Rifampin decreases ceritinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces cevimeline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases chloramphenicol levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces chlordiazepoxide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases chloroquine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin increases cholic acid toxicity by reducing its elimination. Avoid inhibitors of the bile salt efflux pump (BSEP). If coadministration is necessary, monitor liver function tests. Rifampin decreases cilostazol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces cimetidine levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases cinacalcet levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces citalopram levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clofazimine reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases clomipramine levels by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin reduces clonazepam levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin increases clopidogrel metabolism to its active metabolite by inducing CYP3A4. Monitor for increased antiplatelet effects when coadministered with CYP3A4 inducers. Rifampin decreases clorazepate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clotrimazole increases rifampin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of cotrimoxazole increases rifampin levels, potentially increasing toxicity risk. Monitor for adverse reactions. Rifampin decreases clozapine levels by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of therapeutic failure and resistance development. Rifampin decreases cobimetinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers reduce cobimetinib exposure by over 80%, significantly reducing efficacy. Rifampin reduces colchicine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases conivaptan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces conjugated estrogens levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases copanlisib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Rifampin reduces cortisone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases crizotinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Crizotinib increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein efflux. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin reduces cyclophosphamide levels by inducing CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases cyclosporine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Rifampin reduces dabigatran levels by inducing P-glycoprotein efflux. Avoid coadministration. Rifampin decreases dabrafenib levels by increasing its metabolism.
